item.title: ASCO 2026 Highlights
item.description:
• Summary: The ASCO 2026 annual meeting showcased a new era of cancer innovation, but stock market gains were muted for most companies. Notable highlights included daraxonrasib (KRAS G12C inhibitor) and data from Celcuity, which fell despite practice-changing late-stage breast cancer results. Bispecific antibodies and RET fusion-targeting assets in NSCLC drew attention. Other winners included RevMed, Akeso, Summit, and Lilly, while Chinese ADCs continued to feature prominently.
  • MoAs: N/A (multi-asset conference summary)
  • Sources: BioSpace, ApexOnco, ApexOnco, BioSpace, BioSpace, Pharmaceutical Technology

item.title: FDA Actions and Guidance
item.description:
• Summary: The FDA issued a warning letter to Medline over long-running contamination problems, published guidance for pharma on explaining unapproved drugs to payors, and sent an untitled letter to a company over eye-catching graphics in promotional emails. These actions reflect continued regulatory scrutiny across manufacturing, marketing, and communication.
  • MoAs: N/A
  • Sources: BioSpace, Endpoints News, Fierce Pharma

item.title: Highmark Health/HaloMD No Surprises Act
item.description:
• Summary: Highmark Health has sued HaloMD over arbitration disputes under the No Surprises Act, which aims to protect patients from unexpected out-of-network medical bills. The case highlights ongoing challenges in implementing the federal law.
  • MoAs: N/A
  • Sources: STAT News

item.title: China Biotech Deals and Competition
item.description:
• Summary: Chinese biotech companies are facing both pressure and opportunities as dealmaking intensifies. While some US lawmakers express concerns over competition, NextGen biotech leaders argue that collaboration is beneficial. Premiums for Chinese biotech assets are rising as they become more competitive globally.
  • MoAs: N/A
  • Sources: BioPharma Dive, BioSpace, BioSpace

item.title: Pharma Manufacturing Jobs
item.description:
• Summary: A new report projects that pharmaceutical manufacturing will create approximately 19,000 jobs in the US through 2034, driven by reshoring and expansion of domestic production capacity for small molecules and biologics.
  • MoAs: N/A
  • Sources: BioSpace

item.description:
